reasons: isolated harness test: one worker builds the whole program end to end against the owner's acceptance tests (given)

items.title: Scientific calculator (engine and command-line app)
items.goal: Implement the engine and the command-line app so the provided tests pass

card.context: One worker builds the whole program: the engine (src/calc.cpp) and the app on top of it (src/main.cpp). The provided tests are the specification.
card.contract:
ENGINE: Implement double calc::evaluate(const std::string& expr, bool degrees = false), declared in include/calc/calc.hpp and defined in src/calc.cpp. Operators: + - * / % ^ (right associative; binds tighter than unary minus, so -2^2 is -4), postfix ! (factorial), parentheses, unary + and -. Numbers: 12, 1.5, .5, 1.5e2. Constants: pi e tau. One-argument functions: sin cos tan asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh ln log (base 10) log2 sqrt cbrt abs exp floor ceil round fact. Two-argument functions: pow min max. degrees=true makes sin cos tan take degrees and asin acos atan return degrees. Raise std::runtime_error with a clear message on any invalid input (Invalid input raises the error: division or modulo by zero, unknown names or functions, wrong argument count, sqrt of a negative, unbalanced parentheses, a trailing operator, unexpected characters.)
APP: int main(int argc, char** argv). The app takes an expression as its arguments (joined with spaces) or, with none, one line from standard input. It prints the result with 12 significant digits (%.12g) and a newline and exits 0. On invalid input it prints 'Error: ' and the message to standard error and exits non-zero. --degrees sets degrees mode. --screen prints a fixed frame instead: a line of '+' then 38 '-' then '+', a line '| ' + the expression padded to 36 characters + ' |', a line '| = ' + the result padded to 34 characters + ' |' (an error shows as 'Error: message'), and the first rule line again. Evaluate with the engine (double calc::evaluate(const std::string& expr, bool degrees = false), declared in include/calc/calc.hpp and defined in src/calc.cpp).
acceptance: every test in tests/eval.test.cpp and tests/cli.test.cpp passes
C++20, standard library only, no warnings
notes: A small recursive descent parser works well: expression -> term -> unary -> postfix -> primary
